It does not include an ICCM. 104: 105: **Building an FPGA speed optimized model:** 106: Use ``-fpga_optimize=1`` option to ``veer.config`` to build a model that removes clock gating logic from flop model so that the FPGA builds can run at higher speeds. **This is now the default option for targets other than ``typical_pd``.** 107: 108: **Building a Power optimized model (ASIC flows):** 109: Use ``-fpga_optimize=0`` option to ``veer.config`` to build a model that **enables** clock gating logic into the flop model so that the ASIC flows get a better power footprint. **This is now the default option for target``typical_pd``.** 110: 111: This script derives the following consistent set of include files: 112: 113: ./snapshots/default 114: ├── common_defines.vh # `defines for testbench or design 115: ├── defines.h # #defines for C/assembly headers 116: ├── el2_param.vh # Design parameters 117: ├── el2_pdef.vh # Parameter structure 118: ├── pd_defines.vh # `defines for physical design 119: ├── perl_configs.pl # Perl %configs hash for scripting 120: ├── pic_map_auto.h # PIC memory map based on configure size 121: └── whisper.json # JSON file for veer-iss 122: └── link.ld # default linker control file 123: 124: ### Building a model 125: 126: While in a work directory: 127: 128: 1. can be 'verilator' (by default) 'irun' - Cadence xrun, 'vcs' - Synopsys VCS, 'vlog' Mentor Questa 192: 'riviera'- Aldec Riviera-PRO. if not provided, 'make' cleans work directory, builds verilator executable and runs a test. 193: debug=1 - allows VCD generation for verilator and VCS and SHM waves for irun option. 194: assert=1 - enables assertions in simulation runs (with simulators other than Verilator) 195: - predefined CPU configurations 'default' ( by default), 'default_ahb', 'typical_pd', 'high_perf' 196: TEST - allows to run a C (.c) or assembly (.s) test, hello_world is run by default 197: TEST_DIR - alternative to test source directory testbench/asm or testbench/tests 198: - run and build executable model of custom CPU configuration, remember to provide 'snapshot' argument 199: for runs on custom configurations. 200: CONF_PARAMS - allows to provide -set options to veer.conf script to alter predefined EL2 targets parameters 201: ``` 202: 203: Example: 204: 205: ```shell 206: make -f $RV_ROOT/tools/Makefile verilator TEST=cmark 207: ``` 208: 209: will build and simulate the `testbench/asm/cmark.c` program with Verilator. 210: 211: If you want to compile a test only, you can run: 212: 213: ```shell 214: make -f $RV_ROOT/tools/Makefile program.hex TEST= [TEST_DIR=/path/to/dir] 215: ``` 216: 217: The Makefile uses the `snapshot//link.ld` file, generated by the `veer.conf` script by default to build the test executable. 218: User can provide test specific linker file in form `.ld` to build the test executable, 219: in the same directory with the test source. 220: 221: User also can create a test-specific Makefile in `.makefile`, containing building instructions 222: how to create the `program.hex` file used by simulation. The private Makefile should be in the same directory 223: as the test source. See examples in the `testbench/asm` directory. 224: 225: Another way to alter test building process is to use `.mki` file in test source directory. It may help to select multiple sources 226: to compile and/or alter compilation swiches. See examples in the `testbench/tests/` directory 227: 228: *(the `program.hex` file is loaded to instruction and LSU bus memory slaves and optionally to DCCM/ICCM at the beginning of simulation)*. 229: 230: User can build the `program.hex` file by any other means and then run simulation with the following command: 231: 232: ```shell 233: make -f $RV_ROOT/tools/Makefile 234: ``` 235: 236: Note: You may need to delete the `program.hex` file from the work directory, when running a new test. 237: 238: The `$RV_ROOT/testbench/asm` directory contains the following tests ready to simulate: 239: 240: ``` 241: hello_world - default test program to run, prints Hello World message to screen and console.log 242: hello_world_dccm - the same as above, but takes the string from preloaded DCCM. 243: hello_world_iccm - the same as hello_world, but loads the test code to ICCM via LSU to DMA bridge and then executes 244: it from there. Runs on EL2 with AXI4 buses only. 245: cmark - coremark benchmark running with code and data in external memories 246: cmark_dccm - the same as above, running data and stack from DCCM (faster) 247: cmark_iccm - the same as above with preloaded code to ICCM (slower, optimized for size to fit into default ICCM). 248: 249: dhry - Run dhrystone. (Scale by 1757 to get DMIPS/MHZ) 250: ``` 251: 252: The `$RV_ROOT/testbench/hex` directory contains precompiled hex files of the tests, ready for simulation in case RISC-V SW tools are not installed. 253: 254: **Note**: The testbench has a simple synthesizable bridge that allows you to load the ICCM via load/store instructions. This is only supported for AXI4 builds. (End of file - total 254 lines)

Write the following SystemVerilog files for the VeeR EL2 RISC-V core project in /app. These are library primitives that all other modules depend on. Write COMPLETE, FUNCTIONAL implementations.

The design uses these parameters in an `el2_param_t` struct defined in el2_pdef.vh. The struct is instantiated as `parameter el2_param_t pt = ...;` in all modules.

**File 1: /app/design/lib/el2_lib.sv**

This is the main core library providing clock gating cells, flops, and other primitives. It's included via `-y` (library directory), so it contains multiple modules.

Write these modules:
1. `rvoclkhdr` - Positive-latch-style clock gating cell. When FPGA optimization is disabled (pt.FPGA_OPTIMIZE==0), use the latch-based clock gate; otherwise pass clock through. Ports: `(* gated_clk="" *) output logic [WIDTH-1:0] clkout, input logic [WIDTH-1:0] clk, input logic [WIDTH-1:0] en, input logic scan_mode`. Has parameter int WIDTH=1.

2. `rvdff` - parameterized D flip-flop with configurable width.
   Ports: output logic [WIDTH-1:0] dout, input logic [WIDTH-1:0] din, input clk, input rst_l (optional, default 1'b1). Clock only on posedge clk. When rst_l==0, dout=0.
   Also have a version `rvdffe` - same but with enable input `en` (enable when en=1 on posedge).

3. `rvdffs` - D flip-flop with synchronous set. Ports: dout, din, clk, set (1'b0 default, 1'b1 default). When set=1, dout=1 next cycle.

4. `rvdffsc` - D flip-flop with synchronous clear. Ports: dout, din, clk, clear (1'b0 default). When clear=1, dout=0 next cycle.

5. `rvrng` or `rvrangecheck` / `rvbaddrcheck` - range/address check modules used by the core.

6. `rvlsadder` - simple adder

7. `rveven_paritycheck` / `rvodd_paritycheck` / `rveven_paritygen` / `rvecc_decode` / `rvecc_encode` - parity and ECC modules.

8. `rvclkhdr` - same as rvoclkhdr but with different name.

9. `rvpulse` - pulse generator.

10. `rvfunnel` - for funnel shifting.

Write COMPLETE modules. Use the `el2_param_t pt` parameter. All modules should be inside this single file. Make them reasonably functional - not just empty stubs.

IMPORTANT: The NV_FPGA_SYN or FPGA_OPTIMIZE parameter controls whether to use latch clock gates (ASIC style) or pass-through (FPGA style). The test uses fpga_optimize=0, so use latch clock gates.

**File 2: /app/design/lib/beh_lib.sv**

This provides behavioral SRAM models used by DCCM, ICCM, and ICache. It is compiled with `-v` flag (treated as a library file with multiple modules).

Write at minimum these modules:
1. `ram_4096x39` - 4096 deep x 39 wide RAM. Ports: input logic clk, input logic [11:0] addr, input logic [38:0] din, output logic [38:0] dout, input logic we, input logic [38:0] bit_en_vec (bit write enable mask). Also include chip-enable `ce` input.

2. `ram_512x71` - 512 deep x 71 wide RAM (for ICache data). Same port style.

3. `ram_128x25` - 128 deep x 25 wide RAM (for ICache tag). Same port style.

4. `ram_256x34` - 256 deep x 34 wide RAM (for BHT). Same port style.

5. `ram_128x36` - 128 deep x 36 wide RAM (for BTB). Same port style.

Each RAM should use a SystemVerilog array and implement read-before-write or write-first behavior. Use `logic [WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:DEPTH-1];` and always_ff blocks.

**File 3: /app/design/lib/mem_lib.sv**

This provides memory helper cells. Write these modules:
1. `rvbtb_addr_hash` - BTB address hashing
2. `rvbht_addr_hash` - BHT address hashing
3. Various memory-related flops and muxes

**File 4: /app/design/lib/el2_mem_if.sv**

This is the memory export interface that connects the core to external SRAM memories. It's an interface with modports.

Based on the testbench wrapper (`veer_wrapper.sv`), it connects:
- ICCM signals (clken, wren_bank, addr_bank, wr_data, wr_ecc, bank_dout, bank_ecc)
- DCCM signals (clken, wren_bank, addr_bank, wr_data_bank, wr_ecc_bank, bank_dout, bank_ecc)
- ICache data signals (wren, bit_en_vec, wr_data, rw_addr, clken, dout)
- ICache tag signals (clken, wren, wr_data, addr, dout)

Write the interface with these bundles as modports. Use el2_pkg parameter types. The modports needed:
- veer_sram_src (outputs from core): all output ports (clocks, enables, addresses, write data)
- veer_icache_src: all ICache-related output ports
- Opposite direction modports for the SRAM side

Use `parameter el2_param_t pt = ...` for array sizes.

**File 1: /app/design/dmi/dmi_jtag_to_core_sync.v**

This module synchronizes JTAG signals to the core clock domain. It's a simple synchronizer using flip-flops.

Ports:
```
module dmi_jtag_to_core_sync (
    input  logic          jtag_tck,
    input  logic          jtag_tdi,
    input  logic          jtag_tms,
    input  logic          jtag_trst_n,
    input  logic          core_clk,
    input  logic          core_rst_n,
    output logic          jtag_tdo,
    output logic          jtag_tdo_en,

    output logic          dmi_reg_en,

    output logic          dmi_reg_wr,
    output logic [31:0]   dmi_reg_wdata,
    input  logic [31:0]   dmi_reg_rdata,
    output logic          dmi_hard_reset
);
```

Simple implementation: pass-through for most signals, just resynchronize enable/control signals. For simplicity, just wire things through with basic synchronization or direct connection. DMI write/read operations are triggered by TAP controller state machine outputs.

**File 2: /app/design/dmi/rvjtag_tap.v**

This is a JTAG Test Access Port (TAP) controller implementing the standard JTAG state machine (IEEE 1149.1). Simplified implementation.

Ports:
```
module rvjtag_tap (
    input  logic        tck,
    input  logic        tms,
    input  logic        tdi,
    input  logic        trst_n,
    output logic        tdo,
    output logic        tdo_en,
    
    output logic        shift_dr,
    output logic        pause_dr,
    output logic        update_dr,
    output logic        capture_dr,
    
    output logic        shift_ir,
    output logic        pause_ir,
    output logic        update_ir,
    output logic        capture_ir,
    
    output logic [4:0]  tap_state
);
```

Implement the full 16-state JTAG TAP state machine. The states are: TestLogicReset, RunTestIdle, SelectDR, CaptureDR, ShiftDR, Exit1DR, PauseDR, Exit2DR, UpdateDR, SelectIR, CaptureIR, ShiftIR, Exit1IR, PauseIR, Exit2IR, UpdateIR. Drive:
- shift_dr = 1 in ShiftDR state
- update_dr = 1 in UpdateDR state  
- capture_dr = 1 in CaptureDR state
- shift_ir = 1 in ShiftIR state
- update_ir = 1 in UpdateIR state
- capture_ir = 1 in CaptureIR state
- tdo from the shift register
- tdo_en in shift states

**File 3: /app/design/dmi/dmi_wrapper.v**

```
    // DMA debug
```

Write the following SystemVerilog files for the VeeR EL2 RISC-V core in /app. These are the Execution Unit (EXU) modules implementing ALU, multiplier, and divider.

The parameter struct `el2_param_t pt` is available in all modules. The decode packet types are in `el2_pkg` (import el2_pkg::*).

**File 1: /app/design/exu/el2_exu_alu_ctl.sv**

This is the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) control module. It receives decode packets and performs ALU operations.

Module signature:
```systemverilog
module el2_exu_alu_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(
    `include "el2_param.vh"
) (
    input logic          clk,
    input logic          rst_l,
    input logic          free_clk,
    input logic          active_clk,

    input el2_alu_pkt_t  alu_pkt_i,
    input logic [31:0]   rs1_data_i,
    input logic [31:0]   rs2_data_i,
    input logic [31:0]   pc_i,
    input logic [31:0]   imm12_i,
    input logic [31:0]   imm20_i,

    output logic [31:0]  alu_result_o,
    output logic         alu_cmp_o
);
```

The `el2_alu_pkt_t` packet contains fields: add, sub, land, lor, lxor, sll, srl, sra, slt, unsign, beq, bne, blt, bge, jal, clz, ctz, cpop, sext_b, sext_h, min, max, pack, packu, packh, rol, ror, grev, gorc, bset, bclr, binv, bext, sh1add, sh2add, sh3add, zba, zbb, zbs, csr_write, csr_imm, rs1, rs2, imm12, imm20, pc, predict_t, predict_nt.

Implement a combinational ALU that computes:
- ADD/SUB (with carry if needed for sh1add/sh2add/sh3add)
- Logical (AND, OR, XOR)
- Shifts (SLL, SRL, SRA)
- Comparisons (SLT, SLTU, BEQ, BNE, BLT, BGE, BLTU, BGEU)
- Bit manipulation (Zba: sh1add/sh2add/sh3add, Zbb: clz/ctz/cpop/sext_b/sext_h/min/max, Zbs: bset/bclr/binv/bext)
- Other: pack, rol, ror, grev, gorc

Select operands based on control bits (rs1 uses rs1_data_i, rs2 uses rs2_data_i, imm12 uses imm12_i, pc uses pc_i). Pipeline the results with registers.

IMPORTANT: Register the outputs (alu_result_o, alu_cmp_o) with a clocked always_ff block to avoid combinational loops. Use active_clk for gated clock.

**File 2: /app/design/exu/el2_exu_mul_ctl.sv**

Multiplier control module. Performs RV32M multiplication operations.

Module signature:
```systemverilog

#(
    `include "el2_param.vh"
) (
    input logic            clk,
    input logic            rst_l,
    input logic            free_clk,
    input logic            active_clk,
    
    input el2_mul_pkt_t    mul_pkt_i,
    input logic [31:0]     rs1_data_i,
    input logic [31:0]     rs2_data_i,
    
    output logic           mul_ready_o,
    output logic [31:0]    mul_result_o
);
```

The `el2_mul_pkt_t` has: valid, rs1_sign, rs2_sign, low, and bit manipulation Zb* fields.

Implement a multi-cycle multiplier (at least single-cycle for MUL, multi-cycle for MULH/MULHSU/MULHU using shift-add). Use a simple state machine:
- Wait for valid input
- Perform 32-bit multiplication using shift-add algorithm (or simple SystemVerilog `*` operator for single-cycle)
- For signed multiplication: sign-extend operands
- Output when ready

For bitmanip multiply operations (clmul, clmulh, clmulr, grev, gorc, etc.), implement basic versions.

Minimum: use `assign` with `*` operator and register the output.

**File 3: /app/design/exu/el2_exu_div_ctl.sv**

Divider control module. Performs RV32M division operations.

Module signature:
```systemverilog
module el2_exu_div_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(
    `include "el2_param.vh"
) (
    input logic            clk,
    input logic            rst_l,
    input logic            free_clk,
    input logic            active_clk,

    output logic [31:0]    div_result_o
);
```

The `el2_div_pkt_t` has: valid, unsign, rem.

Implement non-restoring division or simple shift-subtract algorithm:
- DIV/DIVU: return quotient
- REM/REMU: return remainder
- Handle division by zero (return -1 for DIV, dividend for REM)
- Handle overflow (INT32_MIN / -1)
- Multi-cycle (at least 4 cycles per bit based on pt.DIV_BIT=4)

Multi-cycle implementation with state machine. The divider processes `pt.DIV_BIT` (=4) bits per cycle using the "new" algorithm (pt.DIV_NEW=1).

**File 4: /app/design/exu/el2_exu.sv**

Top-level EXU module that instantiates and connects alu_ctl, mul_ctl, and div_ctl.

Module signature:
```systemverilog
module el2_exu
import el2_pkg::*;
#(
    `include "el2_param.vh"
) (
    input logic          clk,
    input logic          rst_l,
    input logic          free_clk,
    input logic          active_clk,

```

This module:
1. Generates alu_pkt_o from dec_pkt_i fields (maps decode signals to ALU operations)
2. Generates mul_pkt_o from dec_pkt_i (valid when mul=1)

Simple pipeline register: clock through the IFU outputs to the decode stage. If dec_stall_i, hold values. If !ifu_valid_i, mark dec_valid_o = 0.

**File 3: /app/design/dec/el2_dec_decode_ctl.sv**

Main decode control module. This is the most complex DEC module - it decodes RISC-V instruction formats and generates control signals.

Module signature:
```systemverilog
module el2_dec_decode_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(
    `include "el2_param.vh"
) (
    input logic          clk,
    input logic          rst_l,
    input logic          free_clk,
    input logic          active_clk,
    
    // From instruction buffer
    input logic          dec_valid_i,
    input logic [31:0]   dec_inst_i,
    input logic [31:0]   dec_pc_i,
    input logic [31:0]   dec_npc_i,
    input logic [11:0]   csr_addr_i,
    input logic          csr_wen_i,
    
    // Decode packet output
    output el2_dec_pkt_t dec_pkt_o,
    output el2_reg_pkt_t reg_pkt_o,
    output el2_class_pkt_t class_pkt_o,
    
    // Stall
    output logic         dec_stall_o
);
```

This module decodes the full RV32IMC instruction set. The `el2_dec_pkt_t` contains control signals for ALU operations, CSR access, loads/stores, branches, jumps, multiply/divide, etc.

Key decode logic:
- R-type: funct7 + funct3 + rs1 + rs2 + rd → ALU operation
- I-type: funct3 + opcode → determine if ALU imm, load, CSR, etc.
- S-type: funct3 → store byte/half/word
- B-type: funct3 → branch compare type
- U-type: LUI/AUIPC
- J-type: JAL/JALR
- Compressed (16-bit): decode C instructions to equivalent 32-bit

Extract:
- opcode = dec_inst_i[6:0]
- rd = dec_inst_i[11:7], rs1 = dec_inst_i[19:15], rs2 = dec_inst_i[24:20]
- funct3 = dec_inst_i[14:12], funct7 = dec_inst_i[31:25]
- Immediate decoding for I/S/B/U/J types

For csr operations: if csr_wen_i, decode csr read/write/set/clear.

Output dec_pkt_o with all control signals set appropriately. Output reg_pkt_o with rs1/rs2/rd addresses. Output class_pkt_o with mul/load/alu classification.

Implement:
- CSR register file with key CSRs
- CSR read/write logic decoding csr_addr_i
- Interrupt pending/priority logic
- Trap entry: set mepc, mcause, mtval; redirect PC to mtvec
- MRET: return from trap, restore PC from mepc
- Trace packet generation
- Mcycle/minstret counters

Key CSRs to implement (addresses):
- mvendorid (0xF11): 0x45
- marchid (0xF12): 0x10
- mimpid (0xF13): 0x4
- mhartid (0xF14): 0
- mstatus (0x300): initial 0x1800
- misa (0x301): 0x40001104
- mtvec (0x305): 0
- mscratch (0x340): 0
- mepc (0x341): 0
- mcause (0x342): 0
- mtval (0x343): 0
- mip (0x344): 0
- mie (0x304): 0
- dcsr (0x7b0): 0x40000003

```systemverilog
    output logic [31:0]  rs1_data_o,
    output logic [31:0]  rs2_data_o,
    output logic [31:0]  dec_pc_o,
    output logic [31:0]  dec_npc_o,
    
    // From LSU
    input logic [31:0]   lsu_result_i,
    input logic          lsu_result_valid_i,
    
    // From EXU

    el2_regfile_if.veer_rf_src    rf_src,
    
    // PMP interface
    output el2_pmp_type_pkt_t pmp_type_o,
    output logic          pmp_match_o,

    input logic          dbg_halt_i,
    output logic         dbg_mode_o,

);
```

This top-level module:
1. Instantiates el2_dec_ib_ctl
2. Instantiates el2_dec_decode_ctl
3. Instantiates el2_dec_gpr_ctl
4. Instantiates el2_dec_tlu_ctl
5. Instantiates el2_dec_trigger

8. Handles write-back from EXU/LSU to the register file
9. Computes next PC for branches/jumps
10. Handles interrupt/trap redirection

Key connections:
- IB outputs connect to decode
- Decode generates register addresses for GPR
- GPR provides rs1/rs2 data to EXU
- TLU handles exceptions/interrupts/CSRs
- Write-back from EXU/LSU goes to GPR
- Branch prediction info feeds back to IFU

arguments.prompt:
Write the following SystemVerilog files for the VeeR EL2 RISC-V core in /app. These are the Instruction Fetch Unit (IFU) modules.

The parameter struct `el2_param_t pt` is available. Package `el2_pkg` defines all typedefs. All modules should include `el2_param.vh`. Clock gating with `rvoclkhdr` from el2_lib.

Important reference: the ifu interacts with the AXI bus through a memory bus interface. The bus signals come from the top-level and are forwarded through IFU to the bus controller.

**File 1: /app/design/ifu/el2_ifu_aln_ctl.sv**

Instruction alignment control. Aligns fetched instruction data into proper 32-bit instructions, handling unaligned accesses and compressed (16-bit) instruction boundaries.

```systemverilog
module el2_ifu_aln_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
    input logic         clk, rst_l, free_clk, active_clk,
    input logic [63:0]  fetch_data_i,
    input logic [31:1]  fetch_addr_i,
    input logic         fetch_valid_i,
    input logic         ifc_select_i,
    input logic         cmp_instr_i,
    output logic [31:0] instr_o,
    output logic [31:0] pc_o,
    output logic        valid_o,
    output logic        misaligned_o
);
```

Implement: From 64-bit aligned fetch data, extract 32-bit instruction at offset fetch_addr_i[1]. For compressed instructions (cmp_instr_i=1), extract 16-bit instruction and expand it (pass through as lower 16 bits, upper 16 zeroed). Register the output.

**File 2: /app/design/ifu/el2_ifu_bp_ctl.sv**

Branch prediction control. Implements BTB (Branch Target Buffer), BHT (Branch History Table), and RAS (Return Address Stack).

```systemverilog
module el2_ifu_bp_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
    input logic            clk, rst_l, free_clk, active_clk,
    
    input logic [31:1]     ifc_fetch_addr_i,
    input logic [31:1]     dec_pc_i,
    input logic [31:1]     exu_pc_i,
    input logic            dec_br_redirect_i,
    input logic [31:1]     dec_br_pc_i,
    input logic            exu_br_valid_i,
    input logic [31:1]     exu_br_pc_i,
    input logic            exu_br_error_i,
    input logic            dec_ja_valid_i,
    input logic [31:1]     dec_ja_pc_i,
    
    output el2_br_pkt_t    br_pkt_o,
    output el2_predict_pkt_t predict_pkt_o
);
```

Implement:
- BTB: simple direct-mapped or set-associative buffer storing branch targets. Depth from pt.BTB_ARRAY_DEPTH. Index: fetch_addr_i[pt.BTB_INDEX1_HI:pt.BTB_INDEX1_LO].
- BHT: branch history table for direction prediction. Depth from pt.BHT_ARRAY_DEPTH. 2-bit saturating counters.
- RAS: return address stack. Depth from pt.RET_STACK_SIZE (8). Push on call (JAL rd=x1/x5), pop on return (JALR rd=x0 rs1=x1/x5).
- Predict on fetch; update on decode/execute.
- br_pkt_o: branch prediction packet (valid, toffset, way, ret, prett, etc.)
- predict_pkt_o: prediction details for pipeline use.

For DTIM builds where pt.BTB_ENABLE=0, bypass prediction (always predict not-taken).

**File 3: /app/design/ifu/el2_ifu_compress_ctl.sv**

Compressed instruction decoder. Detects and expands RV32C (16-bit compressed) instructions into equivalent 32-bit instructions.

```systemverilog
module el2_ifu_compress_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
    input logic         clk, rst_l, free_clk, active_clk,
    input logic [31:0]  instr_i,
    input logic         valid_i,
    output logic [31:0] instr_o,
    output logic [31:0] pc_o,
    output logic        valid_o,
    output logic        is_compressed_o
);
```

Detect compressed instruction: if instr_i[1:0] != 2'b11, it's compressed (16-bit). Expand common C instructions:
- C.ADDI4SPN → ADDI rd', x2, nzuimm
- C.LW → LW rd', offset(rs1')
- C.SW → SW rs2', offset(rs1')
- C.ADDI → ADDI rd, rd, imm
- C.JAL → JAL x1, offset (RV32 only)
- C.LI → ADDI rd, x0, imm
- C.LUI → LUI rd, imm
- C.SRLI/SRAI/ANDI → 32-bit equivalents
- C.SUB/XOR/OR/AND → 32-bit equivalents
- C.J → JAL x0, offset
- C.BEQZ → BEQ rs1', x0, offset
- C.BNEZ → BNE rs1', x0, offset
- C.SLLI → SLLI rd, rd, shamt
- C.LWSP → LW rd, offset(x2)
- C.SWSP → SW rs2, offset(x2)
- C.MV → ADD rd, x0, rs2
- C.ADD → ADD rd, rd, rs2
- C.JR → JALR x0, rs1, 0
- C.JALR → JALR x1, rs1, 0
- C.EBREAK → EBREAK
- C.NOP → ADDI x0, x0, 0

**File 4: /app/design/ifu/el2_ifu_ifc_ctl.sv**

Instruction fetch control. Manages the fetch state machine, fetch address generation, and stall control.

```systemverilog
module el2_ifu_ifc_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
    input logic            clk, rst_l, free_clk, active_clk,
    
    // Control inputs
    input logic [31:1]     rst_vec_i,
    input logic            dec_stall_i,
    input logic            dec_br_redirect_i,
    input logic [31:1]     dec_br_pc_i,
    input logic            exu_br_error_i,
    input logic [31:1]     exu_br_pc_i,
    
    // Branch prediction
    input el2_br_pkt_t     br_pkt_i,
    
    // Memory interface response
    input logic            mem_valid_i,
    input logic [63:0]     mem_data_i,
    input logic            mem_error_i,
    
    // Fetch outputs
    output logic           fetch_req_o,
    output logic [31:1]    fetch_addr_o,
    output logic [31:1]    next_fetch_addr_o,
    output logic [63:0]    fetch_data_o,
    output logic [31:1]    fetch_pc_o,
    output logic           fetch_valid_o,
    output logic           fetch_cmp_o
);
```

Implement:
- Fetch FSM: IDLE → REQ → WAIT → DONE
- On reset: load rst_vec_i as initial PC
- On each cycle where not stalled: request next fetch address
- When mem_valid_i received: latch fetch data and advance PC
- On branch redirect: override fetch address with branch target
- On branch mispredict (exu_br_error_i): redirect to correct PC
- Generate next_fetch_addr_o = fetch_addr + 4 (or predicted target if branch predicted taken)
- fetch_cmp_o indicates compressed instruction boundary

**File 5: /app/design/ifu/el2_ifu_mem_ctl.sv**

IFU memory control. Manages AXI/AHB memory interface for instruction fetches.

```systemverilog
module el2_ifu_mem_ctl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
```

Write the following SystemVerilog files for the VeeR EL2 RISC-V core in /app. These are the top-level integration modules that tie together the IFU, DEC, EXU, LSU, PIC, DMA, PMP, and debug subsystems.

The parameter struct `el2_param_t pt` is available. All modules import `el2_pkg::*` and `include "el2_param.vh"`. Use clock gating with `rvoclkhdr` from el2_lib.

**File 1: /app/design/el2_pic_ctrl.sv**

PIC (Programmable Interrupt Controller). Handles external interrupt sources, prioritization, and delivery.

```systemverilog
module el2_pic_ctrl
import el2_pkg::*;
#(`include "el2_param.vh") (
    input logic           clk, rst_l, free_clk, active_clk,
    
    // Interrupt inputs from outside
    input logic [pt.PIC_TOTAL_INT:1] extintsrc_req_i,
    
    // Core interface  
    output logic          pic_interrupt_o,
    output logic [7:0]    pic_claimid_o,
    
    // LSU access (memory-mapped PIC registers)
    input logic           pic_req_i,
    input logic           pic_write_i,
    input logic [31:0]    pic_addr_i,
    input logic [31:0]    pic_wdata_i,
    output logic          pic_ack_o,
    output logic [31:0]   pic_rdata_o
);
```

PIC memory map (offset from pt.PIC_BASE_ADDR = 0xf00c0000):
- 0x0000: MEIPL (priority level) - one per interrupt source [pt.PIC_TOTAL_INT:1]
- 0x1000: MEIP (interrupt pending) - read-only status
- 0x2000: MEIE (interrupt enable) - one per source
- 0x3000: MPICCFG (PIC configuration) 
- 0x3004: MEIPT (priority threshold)
- 0x4000: MEIGWCTRL (gateway control)
- 0x5000: MEIGWCLR (gateway clear)

Implement:
- Register file for all PIC registers
- External interrupt synchronization
- Priority comparison: if any enabled interrupt has MEIPL > MEIPT, assert pic_interrupt_o
- Claim ID/Capture on interrupt acknowledge: store highest priority pending interrupt ID
- Register read/write via pic_addr_i decode (word-aligned addresses)
- Parameterized for pt.PIC_TOTAL_INT (31)
- pic_claimid_o = index of highest priority pending interrupt

Simple implementation: single bank of registers for each function. Interrupt pending registers are set by extintsrc_req_i and cleared on service.
